-- Alternative approach: use a cross join to create order-slot combinations,
-- then use window functions to compute cumulative picks

WITH fifo_inv AS (
    SELECT 
        i.product_id,
        i.qty as inv_qty,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY i.product_id 
            ORDER BY p.purchased ASC, i.qty ASC, i.id ASC
        ) as inv_rn
    FROM inventory i
    JOIN purchases p ON i.purchase_id = p.id
),
orderlines_ordered AS (
    SELECT 
        ol.order_id,
        ol.product_id,
        CAST(ol.qty AS DOUBLE) as required_qty,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY ol.product_id 
            ORDER BY ol.order_id ASC, ol.id ASC
        ) as order_rn
    FROM orderlines ol
),
-- Get max order_rn and max inv_rn per product
product_bounds AS (
    SELECT 
        o.product_id,
        MAX(o.order_rn) as max_order_rn,
        (SELECT MAX(inv_rn) FROM fifo_inv f WHERE f.product_id = o.product_id) as max_inv_rn
    FROM orderlines_ordered o
    GROUP BY o.product_id
),
-- Generate all order-slot pairs for each product
all_pairs AS (
    SELECT 
        o.product_id,
        o.order_rn,
        o.required_qty,
        f.inv_rn,
        f.inv_qty
    FROM orderlines_ordered o
    JOIN product_bounds pb ON o.product_id = pb.product_id
    JOIN fifo_inv f ON f.product_id = o.product_id AND f.inv_rn <= pb.max_inv_rn
    WHERE o.order_rn <= pb.max_order_rn
),
-- Now compute which slots are consumed by which orders
-- This is complex - let me try a different approach using cumulative sums

-- For each product, compute the cumulative inventory and cumulative demand
-- and find the crossover point

cumul_inv AS (
    SELECT 
        product_id,
        inv_rn,
        SUM(inv_qty) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY inv_rn) as cumul_inv
    FROM fifo_inv
),
cumul_demand AS (
    SELECT 
        product_id,
        order_rn,
        SUM(required_qty) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY order_rn) as cumul_demand
    FROM orderlines_ordered
)
